finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-supplied params[:state] through Base64.decode64 into Marshal.load, allowing remote code execution via a crafted Marshal payload.
finding.source: app.rb:5-6, params[:state] from the HTTP request (unauthenticated)

trace.note: params[:state] -> Base64.decode64 -> Marshal.load (no signature, class allowlist, or size limit)

finding.guards_checked: No authentication on the route, no HMAC/signature on the blob, no class allowlist, no size limit, no safe loader. POST /import (app.rb:10-13) uses JSON.parse, which is not code execution, so SAFE. GET /health (app.rb:15-17) returns a constant, SAFE.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5-6 has no before-filter, auth check, HMAC/signature verification, class allowlist, or size limit between params[:state] and Marshal.load. The directory contains only app.rb, so no middleware or config.ru applies one.
verdict.reason: At app.rb:6, the unauthenticated POST /restore route (app.rb:5) passes params[:state] through Base64.decode64 into Marshal.load with no guard, so an anonymous attacker can supply a crafted Marshal payload for code execution.
